Each analysis below is a reproducible document: the methods, the code that ran
them, and the output in one place.

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.analysis-card}
### [HTE analysis pipeline](hte-pipeline.qmd)

Conditional average treatment effects estimated with BART, subgroups discovered
by fitting a tree to those estimates, sensitivity to the prior and to other
estimators, heterogeneity by prognostic score, and randomization-based bounds on
the distribution of individual effects.

Outcome observed for everyone.
:::

::: {.analysis-card}
### [SACE and CSACE using BART](sace-csace.qmd)

Treatment effects on outcomes truncated by death, estimated among
always-survivors, with the same fit-the-fit approach applied to the estimated
conditional effects. Applied to the ARDS Network ARMA trial.

Outcome observable only in survivors.
:::

:::

## Reusing this work

The analyses share a few components:

- **Multi-chain BART** — [`clusterfunctions.R`](../code/clusterfunctions.R),
  which runs several `BART` chains in parallel and collects them into one
  posterior.
- **Randomization-based ITE inference** — the `RIQITE` package with the helper
  functions from
  [Enhanced inference for ITE quantiles](https://github.com/Zhe-Chen-1999/Enhanced_inference_for_ITE_quantiles).

The [tutorial](../tutorial.qmd) walks through running the HTE pipeline on a new
trial. If you would like help applying any of this to a trial of your own, please
[get in touch](../people.qmd).
